{"status":"active","summary":"Elian wants to keep the old patrol road safe without turning Brackenford into a frightened military camp. He is quietly determined to learn why the goblins are moving inward.","visibility":"party"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Sella wants the Hearthside Inn to remain a place where patrols, travelers, and villagers can find warmth without being asked to surrender their hope. She notices every stranger and remembers every kindness.","visibility":"party"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Waystone at Brackenford","premise":"In a warm frontier village beside a smaller, ancient forest, a lull in goblin attacks and a forgotten waystone cellar hint that something old is waking beneath the trees.","partyGoals":["Build trust with the people of Brackenford and learn what has changed along the old patrol road.","Follow the clues toward the waystone cellar without losing sight of the village\u0027s safety."],"toneAndBoundaries":["Cozy high fantasy with poetic scenery, kind communities, and space for quiet relationships.","Mysteries, riddles, hidden quests, and occasional frightening danger are welcome; player choices matter and companions are not disposable."],"rulesetScope":"dnd2024","creationMethod":"manual","reviewFingerprint":"202dd66937c5d91d84cbb41a6f84dc5acea70cdb5282dcdb2fb22b5e25ccce6e"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Waking Depths","partyStake":"The village\u0027s peace and the fragile trust between its people, patrols, and the forest depend on understanding what is waking before it reaches the surface."}
{"status":"active","title":"Brackenford Arrivals","partyQuestion":"Why have the goblins stopped raiding outward, and what is waiting beneath the old waystone cellar?"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The current approximately 2,000-year age began with the formation of the Thalmos Empire.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalorien\u0027s ages are of broadly similar length, approximately 2,000 years each.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Settlements around the continent, including settlements inhabited by species other than humans, existed before recorded history and before the Thalmos Empire. During the monster outbreak they helped save humanity and were granted amnesty in return. The kingdoms later continued to respect that protection partly out of reverence and partly from superstition about whether violating peace with the other races would anger spirits or gods.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Most people know the previous bad age through stories told by ancestors rather than personal experience.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The ancient defensive dungeons were created during an era that flourished roughly 4,000\u20136,000 years ago. There is not enough research to establish that any surviving dungeon is older than that range. The builders were aware of the monsters beneath the ground and built the complexes as a defensive measure against them.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"In the mostly forgotten ancient language of Thalorien, -on is a personal-name ending and -os is a place-name ending. Thalmon becomes Thalmos under this convention. Thalorien is a later name for the world derived from the same linguistic root rather than a direct ancient place-name.","provenance":"Approved ancient-language naming revision from the world-creation conversation (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Across Thalos, settlements inhabited by species other than humans are older than recorded history and did not form with the Thalmos Empire. Some survived the monster invasion better than later civilizations and became important keepers of guarded historical memory.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The seven rulers agreed to convene once each year in the eldest sibling\u0027s kingdom. Any ruler could offer advice, but each kingdom\u0027s ruler retained final authority to accept or reject it. Their shared purpose remained preserving Thalmon\u0027s dream of peace and utopian prosperity.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"During the great war, the School of the Arts and Entertainment, preserved in honor of the slain Prince of the Arts, was destroyed. Teachers and students salvaged what they could and dispersed across Thalos.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Ashen Crown Isles are Waylos\u0027s offshore volcanic island chain beyond Mount Cinderwake.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Bannerfall Tower is Valeros\u0027s destroyed magic tower: a forbidden, dangerous ruin in the Oathshield Range that remains reachable.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The existence, nature, and extent of lands beyond Thalos are unknown rather than established as nonexistent.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"After the great Thalos war, a shared Book of Truth was created to teach every citizen their rights and responsibilities and to preserve stories of history and the dangers of war.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Book of Truth stood in the way of the merchants\u0027 consumer manipulation because its history, warnings about war, and teaching about rights and responsibilities encouraged citizens to question unfair arrangements.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"Superseded working name. After the great Thalos war, a shared Book of Wisdom was created to teach every citizen their rights and responsibilities and to preserve stories of history and the dangers of war.","provenance":"Archived during the world-creation interview when the canonical name was clarified as the Book of Truth (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Brackenford is a Valeros frontier village beside a smaller, ancient forest. Its inn, shrine, smith, small market, patrol traffic, timber trade, and frontier supplies make it a natural local starting setting.","provenance":"Approved as a local starting setting during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"At first, attempts to seal the underground monster caves caused new caves to appear. Sealing the largest caves did not produce new ones, but sealing smaller caves caused new caves to appear elsewhere.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Churches, clerics, and priests were entrusted with spreading the Book of Wisdom as a civic peace duty separate from their religious responsibilities. In return, the kingdoms granted the churches greater authority and freedom.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Churches possessed authority of their own in relation to the gods. The gods are the gods that exist in D\u0026D 5e; which are prominent in Thalos and how worship varies remain to be detailed. Churches often trained clerics who helped heal the sick, and this religious healing network was institutionally distinct from expensive university-trained arcane magicians.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The kingdoms made sustained efforts to teach their citizens to reject waging war, seeking a broad civic agreement that war must never again be chosen between the kingdoms.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}
{"status":"active","summary":"The known world contains one known continent, Thalos.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Creatures of legend exist in Thalorien: beings so rare that most knowledge of them comes through folklore, old stories, disputed sightings, and legend.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Crownmere is the capital of Aldros, lying east of the World Tree Grounds.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S3 location proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Some historians believe the present age may now be approaching its end, but this is a scholarly interpretation rather than an established certainty.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Dark Market is the historical origin of Thalos\u0027s black markets and organized underworld; it grew from the secret knowledge and research networks created by persecuted magicians from the fallen tower.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Dawnbell Tower is Rhiannos\u0027s active magic tower, associated with healing, refuge, and the joining of divine and arcane learning.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Over the following centuries, the seven kingdoms developed distinct cultures. Each kingdom also developed its own customs and rules for lineage, succession, and determining who would rule.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The ancient dungeons used maze-like structures to confuse monsters trying to escape into the overworld. They also contained traps and supply chests for intelligent peoples who descended to eliminate excess monsters.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"After the ancient wards were placed and the dungeons were forgotten, the monsters inside grew stronger and more numerous over at least 4,000 years while the wards gradually weakened.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Dwarves live mostly in the mountains and were better equipped to protect themselves and their history from the monster invasion.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"After Thalmon died, all eight of his children inherited power together and attempted to govern through the cooperative council structure he had prepared for them.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Elaris is the great Elven settlement around the World Tree. Its historians, called the Keepers of the Long Remembrance, preserve living recollections and guarded records reaching farther back than any human kingdom\u0027s history.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Elven society has the longest lifespan among the surviving peoples and guards historical memory better than any other culture.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"After the great Thalos war, the settlements\u2014especially the elves\u2014reminded the kingdoms of Thalmon\u0027s dream, his wisdom, and the old constitution that had been meant to guard peace.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Emberwright Tower is Waylos\u0027s active magic tower, associated with engineering, craft, and the careful creation of useful things.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The great war broke one of the four magical towers, leaving it abandoned. Its battle magicians scattered across Thalos and were widely feared because of their knowledge of battle magic; other kingdoms feared they might reunite and stage an uprising.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Minevros, Valeros, Rhiannos, and Waylos each had a magic tower.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon founded four magical towers as independent sources of authority. The towers were empowered to challenge or veto imperial decisions when future rulers violated Thalmon\u0027s constitution.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The four towers trained magicians specifically for combat, separating battle magic from ordinary magical education so the towers could oppose an unlawful ruler and limit uncontrolled access to combat magic that might enable uprisings.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The current post-Thalmos age is the best documented period of Thalorien\u0027s history. There are fragments of knowledge about the world before the kingdoms and the Thalmos Empire, but the monster invasion destroyed much of it, and the oldest surviving records are closely guarded by long-lived or well-protected settlements.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Settlements near forests, mountains, or other monster-haunted reaches share responsibility for local safety. Patrols, watch posts, warning bells, and trained monster-hunters form a practical safety net, while communities try to preserve ordinary life instead of becoming permanent military camps.","provenance":"Authored by Codex at the user\u0027s request (2026-08-22); clearly distinguishable from user-confirmed canon and open to later revision.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The ancient monster wards eventually waned and failed, causing the great monster invasion. No such wards remain active today. The invasion was especially damaging to humanity because monster populations had grown while human defensive capabilities had atrophied during the long period of safety.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"By the end of roughly the fourth century of the current age, power among the seven kingdoms had become increasingly unequal. Respect for the old imperial constitution no longer provided enough diplomatic cohesion, and a massive war began that eventually encompassed all seven kingdoms.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The great Thalos war ended more than 1,530 years ago. Its losses and lessons are now separated from living memory by many generations.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Greenmantle is Valeros\u0027s great western forest. Valeros patrols its goblin-haunted interior, and the other kingdoms compensate it for maintaining that frontier.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Harrowfall\u0027s access to the mountain range and cold weather allowed it to freeze and preserve much more of its supplies for sale during the off-season, giving it a major advantage over Merrowgate.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"During the great Thalos war, the allied forces of Merceros and Valeros destroyed the trade city of Harrowfall.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Harrowfall is the ruined northern trade city of Evandos, beside the distinct Northern Cold Highlands.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S3 location proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"No one can enter Harrowfall now. The ruined trade city remains occupied and guarded by the evil spirits that settled there after the massacre.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Merceros\u0027s ruler, driven by greed, ordered the troops to slaughter every living being in Harrowfall after the city had been defeated.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Harrowfall\u0027s historic cold-weather trade advantage came from access to a separate northern highland range, not from Valeros\u0027s southeastern mountains.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview; Slice S2 geographic default accepted when the user instructed continuation (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Before its destruction, Harrowfall had become much more prosperous than Merrowgate. This embarrassed Merceros, a commerce-oriented kingdom, while Evandos was known for being founded on law and order.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The resentment, despair, and sorrow left lingering in Harrowfall welcomed evil spirits. The spirits feasted on the dead and settled in the ruined city.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Six kingdoms form a hexagonal ring around central Aldros: Minevros northwest, Evandos north, Rhiannos northeast, Valeros southeast, Merceros south, and Waylos southwest. Minevros and Valeros oppose one another across Aldros.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"As the networks expanded and attracted followers beyond the original magicians, they became a broader hidden society outside or partially outside ordinary institutions. Trade routes for forbidden knowledge expanded into trade in other prohibited or illicit goods and services.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The scattered battle magicians were hunted. To survive, many hid their identities and lived as travellers, merchants, nomads, entertainers, or under other disguises.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The council\u0027s persistent indecisiveness caused the empire to stagnate. Government became unable to respond effectively to problems, and ordinary people increasingly suffered.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon\u0027s empire maintained a system of welfare intended to support the population. Its exact programs, funding, eligibility, and survival in the modern kingdoms remain to be established.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalos contains small independent settlements, many inhabited by species other than humans and older than recorded history. They predate the Thalmos Empire rather than forming with it. They are especially found between borders and occasionally as enclaves; although too small and weak to be recognized as countries, they may maintain their own laws, traditions, local government, and, rarely, currency.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Kharad Veyr is a venerable Dwarven mountain settlement whose archivists maintain the Deep Ledger, a tradition of recording craft, lineage, treaties, and remembered dangers in stone and metal. The Ledger preserves fragments of history that survived the monster invasion.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Four siblings received kingdoms containing one of the four magical towers. The eldest sibling, trained in diplomacy and administration, received the central inland kingdom containing the University. The two remaining siblings received kingdoms centered on the empire\u0027s two major trade hubs.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The seven kingdoms have known genuine peace for generations, but their relationships vary: some have excellent relationships and close ties, while others have political, economic, territorial, or historical tensions. No kingdom is currently preparing for war and war is not inevitable.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Some kingdoms have political tensions with one another, but no war is currently brewing.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Alongside standard D\u0026D magic, Thalorien has local magical traditions known as knot magic and magical music. Their methods, limits, cultural origins, and relationship to university magic remain open questions for later exploration.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalos is the limit of the known world, not necessarily the limit of Thalorien. No confirmed lands beyond Thalos are known and the oceans beyond the continent remain largely uncharted.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Larkspire University is Thalmon\u0027s historic university, west of the World Tree Elven Enclave in Aldros.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S3 location proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalorien has a rich, layered history made up of multiple eras, obscure cultures, secrets, and ancient structures whose purposes most people no longer understand.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"As the story begins, the leaders of the seven kingdoms are interested in what the merchants are proposing, making the coalition\u0027s campaign a quiet threat to the foundations of the current peace.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Thalorien is in a long, peaceful era.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"With every transition into a new age, more of the past is lost. The oldest ages survive only in fragments: ruins, artifacts, partial records, traditions, and mysteries whose original meanings may no longer be known.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Some cultures teach their own magical traditions outside universities. These practitioners usually remain within their communities, though exceptions occur.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Magic exists in Thalorien and virtually everyone has witnessed some form of magic at least once, but it is not abundant in ordinary life. Most material life, work, travel, and institutions remain recognizably medieval; magic supplements them rather than replacing ordinary labor at scale.","provenance":"User-established worldbuilding constraint; recorded and clarified by Codex (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Ordinary villages generally cannot afford a resident magician. Exceptions include unusually wealthy or strategically valuable settlements, such as communities built around rare resources or mines or settlements with many warriors who fight monsters and justify stationed magical healers.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Deliberate spellcasting usually requires costly education, with universities as the dominant formal route. Students commonly come from noble or well-off families or must earn enough afterward to repay the cost.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Everyday society and material life in Thalorien remain broadly medieval despite the existence of magic.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The king of Merceros could not tolerate the embarrassment of Harrowfall becoming more prosperous than Merrowgate, despite Merceros\u0027s identity as a commerce-oriented kingdom.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The king of Merceros decided that there should be only one major trade hub from then on, and ordered the attack on Harrowfall to eliminate his commercial rival.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Merceros lies to the south of the World Tree region, while Evandos lies to its north.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"During the great Thalos war, Merceros joined with its neighbor Valeros in a military alliance.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"About 150 years ago, merchants in Thalorien\u0027s main trading hub grew strong and bold enough to form a secret coalition.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"After learning to influence vendors and markets, the merchant coalition sought to influence consumers as well, so people would accept worse deals without recognizing how they were being manipulated.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The secret merchant coalition began by exchanging market advice and industry knowledge, but that cooperation quickly evolved into manipulating the market as a whole.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The merchants plan to influence the kingdoms by arguing that roughly 1,500 years have passed since the Book of Truth was released, that the danger of war is gone, and that its peace education has become harmful indoctrination that prevents free minds, progress, and new ideas.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The current peace is quietly threatened by a secret merchant coalition seeking to weaken the shared civic education that protects citizens from manipulation, while persuading the kingdoms that this safeguard is obsolete.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Merrowgate is the surviving southern trade city of Merceros.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S3 location proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The royal family maintained a Military School as an extension of the University. The University educated commanders in the art of warfare, including command and strategy, while the Military School focused on practical fighting techniques and martial training.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The nations that lost so much in the great Thalos war have replaced its old points of interest with newer ones over the centuries. In the present day, the seven nations are more balanced than they were when the war began.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"During his travels, Thalmon discovered that the monsters were coming from caves beneath the ground.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Monster wards capable of preventing creatures from entering the overworld were discovered about 4,000 years ago. The wards were placed on the dungeons, after which the dungeons were forgotten because they were no longer needed. No such wards remain active today.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Mount Cinderwake is the great volcano of Waylos\u0027s Southwestern Volcanic Region.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Nethravai were the civilization that created the oldest known dungeons between roughly 4,000 and 6,000 years ago. They built maze-like complexes to contain monsters from the deep caves and later developed monster wards that kept those creatures from reaching the overworld. Their own history, name, and culture remain only partly understood.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Toward the northeastern kingdom, the land grows more heavily forested. In the kingdom\u0027s far north, the forests give way to snow and cold mountain country.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Oathshield Range is Valeros\u0027s southeastern mountain range, named for the kingdom\u0027s defensive founding purpose.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"During the unrest, Prince Oberon, the Prince of the Arts, was killed. His death shocked the seven survivors into acting decisively, and they moved hastily to quell the rebellion.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Peace is a central value of Thalorien.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Enough time has passed that most people are accustomed to living in peace.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The known continent of Thalos contains the seven kingdoms of Thalorien.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"For roughly the first 1,500 years after the Thalmos Empire was divided, the seven kingdoms used the same currency. They later adopted separate local currencies after realizing that Evandos, in the north, had access to metals from its Northern Cold Highlands that were scarce elsewhere. Rather than let the northern kingdom control the common currency or pay it for access to those metals, the kingdoms chose distinct local metal compositions for their currencies. Even after Evandos lost the trade hub of Harrowfall during the great war, it could rely on coin production from the northern mountains until roughly 500 years ago.","provenance":"Corrected during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"After the rebellion, the seven surviving siblings kept the council but divided the Thalmos Empire into seven countries, one ruled by each sibling. The division was made as fairly as they could manage so each new kingdom possessed a major source of value and authority.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The eight siblings did not get along. Their specialized educations, intended to make their expertise complementary, instead steered them toward different priorities and perspectives, and they struggled to agree on imperial decisions.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Farther north in the same broad southeastern region, the terrain becomes Mediterranean-like, with forests, agricultural fields, villages, and the capital. This settled belt forms a gentler transition between the tropical south and colder northern lands.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The southeastern part of the continent is marked by high tropical cliffs and deep tropical jungle valleys. The cliffs divide the region into dramatic heights and sheltered green depths, with many places still difficult to reach.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Southwestern Volcanic Region, including its volcano and offshore volcanic island chain, lies within Waylos\u0027s territory.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview; Slice S2 geographic default accepted when the user instructed continuation (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"A volcano stands in the southwestern part of the continent, with a group of volcanic islands lying offshore. The surrounding southwestern region also includes a broad desert shaped by the volcano\u0027s heat, ash, and rain shadow.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalorien uses the standard D\u0026D gods, planes, and divine order as its underlying reality. Local churches and peoples worship and interpret those gods through their own traditions; ancient cultures preserve different creation myths and beliefs about death, and contradictory evidence can make true history difficult to reconstruct.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Starwell Tower is Minevros\u0027s active magic tower, devoted to scholarship, observation, and long records.","provenance":"Approved as a Slice S4 regional proposal during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The great monster invasion that preceded the founding of the Thalmos Empire was called The Sudden Calamity.","provenance":"Confirmed during the world-creation interview (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon was widely beloved during his reign and faced no significant organized opposition, giving him unusual freedom to reshape the empire and develop what he personally considered a utopian society.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon established a constitution intended to constrain future imperial rulers.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon had eight children: six sons and two daughters. He educated each in a different domain of knowledge required for governing, intending them to rule cooperatively as a council and combine their expertise for the prosperity of the empire.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon named the Thalmos Empire after himself. The modern names Thalos for the continent and Thalorien for the world derive from an ancient language now forgotten by almost everyone; knowledge of that language survives primarily among some scholars and the imperial lineage.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon\u0027s overriding political goal was the preservation of peace. He believed lasting peace depended on creating happy, capable citizens, and his education, welfare, religious, administrative, commercial, infrastructural, constitutional, and military reforms were intended to support that goal.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon founded one university intended to teach the population the accumulated fields of learning available in the empire. At its founding it was open to everyone.","provenance":"Imported from updated World_Creation_Ledger.md (2026-08-22).","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Thalmon\u0027s society is not canonically established as an objective utopia. {"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Bellafont is a kingdom of Eredane. Its present pressure: An orchard blight and rival claims over irrigation monasteries strain a famously charming court.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Carrowmere is a kingdom of Eredane. Its present pressure: Shipwright labour disputes threaten the grain fleet before a dangerous sailing season.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Dunmarrow is a kingdom of Eredane. Its present pressure: Iron wealth declines while border forts and old military families demand more funding.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Kethria is a kingdom of Solasca. Its present pressure: Copper tithe records suggest someone has paid a sleeping dragon for generations.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Lornesse is a kingdom of Eredane. Its present pressure: Mine closures expose older tunnels, unpaid obligations, and possible dragon signs.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Namarra is a kingdom of Solasca. Its present pressure: Delta villages vanish from tax rolls while their grain still appears in foreign markets.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Ordelain is a kingdom of Solasca. Its present pressure: River law and royal law conflict after the Aur changes course around a wealthy estate.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Selucia is a island kingdom of Solasca. Its present pressure: A royal wedding could settle maritime claims, if the families, sailors, weather, and missing cook cooperate.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Seven Lamps League is a merchant city league of Solasca. Its present pressure: The League\u0027s rotating chair has disappeared with the key to a sealed Concord archive.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Tessarane is a kingdom of Solasca. Its present pressure: Astronomers predict an ordinary comet; the court insists it confirms three incompatible prophecies.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Veyr Marches is a elective march confederacy of Eredane. Its present pressure: The High Warden is dying and the marches disagree whether one successor should command them all.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Dunwarren controls the eastern forest roads and supplies beams, charcoal, carts, and bow staves. Its walls incorporate living oaks protected by charter, making maintenance both impressive and botanically argumentative.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Highmead stands on a defensible chalk ridge above sheep country. It is known for wool halls, teacher-priests, legal schools, large skies, and citizens who regard climbing the hill as evidence of moral seriousness.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Merecross grew where the Mere meets the Lark and Weir rivers. Barges, paper, apples, wool, court business, and bridge tolls feed a city of stone quays and timber upper stories. Its seven public bridges are maintained by different institutions, producing beautiful views and spectacularly petty jurisdiction disputes.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"The capital terraces down orchard hills toward a palace, cathedral gardens, cloth halls, fountains, and a river lined with laundry platforms. Manners are polished; civic debates are not.","visibility":"public"}
{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Cresset is a textile and dye city where canals turn fulling mills and entire streets change colour with the day\u0027s work.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Vintner\u0027s Reach controls southern wine roads, barrel making, river barges, and hillside reservoirs. Its guild feasts are legendary and its hangovers legally irrelevant.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Gullstrand\u0027s vast yards build and repair deep-water ships. The city smells of oak, tar, hot metal, salt, and communal kitchens run by craft fraternities.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Penross clings to western cliffs around a natural harbour and a renowned school of navigation, weather, law, and rescue medicine.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Saltmere stands on tidal islands joined by stone causeways and movable timber bridges. Royal offices share space with fish markets, salt warehouses, rescue houses, and legal chambers specialising in things that floated away.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"The capital crowns a black basalt ridge above two peat rivers. Its fortress, iron exchange, winter courts, and roofed market make it severe from a distance; inside, painted doors, heated benches, and competitive soup reveal a more domestic city.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Moorwatch began as a frontier fort and became a borough of peat cutters, shepherds, horse breeders, and military pensioners. Its straight streets end abruptly in bog.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Stonewake is a northern port built behind a long breakwater of fitted dark stone. Ore, smoked fish, timber, and soldiers pass through it; so do rumours from beyond the Greyward Ocean.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Copperdeep descends through terraces around ancient mine mouths, smelters, baths, chapels, and workers\u0027 halls. Upper galleries are active; lower levels have been sealed for generations.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"This pass city controls caravans, mountain rescue, and the safest eastern crossing. Houses cluster behind snow walls and connect through covered lanes.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Lorn fills a hanging valley beneath the royal monastery-fortress. Bells coordinate markets, avalanches, funerals, fire, court sessions, and lunch with patterns outsiders routinely confuse.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Oakshield guards forest passes with layered timber walls designed to be repaired, not admired. It exports horses, charcoal, leather, and excellent preserved mushrooms.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Redgate surrounds the rust-red stone arch where nine march roads meet. The High Warden\u0027s moot, escort market, banner court, and sprawling inns make it a capital only when everyone agrees.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Vanner\u0027s Rest grew around caravan fields and is famous for wheelwrights, horse doctors, roadside theatre, and the loudest inn signs in Eredane.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Copperwell serves mines, smelters, metalworkers, and caravan brokers. Its deep communal well is lined with donation plaques spanning four centuries.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Snowgate controls the northern pass and its avalanche shelters. Summer markets are brief and intense; winter life moves into connected stone halls.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"The capital occupies terraces above the confluence of three snowmelt canals. Copper roofs, carved doors, council courts, wrestling grounds, and fruit gardens define the city.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Namar rises on islands and embankments where the delta branches. Boats are ordinary transport; addresses include both street and nearest landing.","visibility":"public"}
{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Reedcrown guards royal granaries, seed stores, canal gates, and flood reserves behind immense reed and brick embankments.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Saffron Quay is a warm-water export port for spice, cloth, rice, fish, and delta craft. Warehouses stand on pilings, and tide marks are painted as civic records.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Aurent spans both banks of the Aur with broad quays, palaces, law schools, grain exchanges, shaded courts, and public fountains. River cases can make or end political careers.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Malvar is the kingdom\u0027s granary city and cattle market, built around enormous brick storehouses and a temple distribution complex.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Vessa makes paper from river reeds and houses private, royal, temple, and commercial archives. Its streets are shaded by cloth awnings and patrolled aggressively for fire.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Candleport climbs around a protected harbour beneath the royal citadel. Pilgrim bells, fishing boats, citrus markets, coffee houses, embassies, and parliament stairs crowd the waterfront.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Mariselle is an artistic and commercial port of tile workshops, theatres, rope yards, music schools, and crowded hillside neighbourhoods.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Saint Orro surrounds a fortified pilgrimage monastery and the islands\u0027 largest repair dock. The saint is remembered for rescuing enemies and criticizing their knots.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Aster Quay is the League\u0027s diplomatic and financial centre, built around seven harbour basins and the sealed hall where the Lantern Concord ended. Printing houses, embassies, insurers, warehouses, and cafes fill narrow streets.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Glassharbor produces windows, mirrors, lenses, beads, bottles, and elaborate navigational lights. Its furnaces glow along a sheltered bay.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Low Lantern occupies marshy islands at the northern strait. Warehouses, rope bridges, customs houses, and cheap lodging make it less grand and more useful than the other League cities.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Blue Step sits where the plateau road descends through blue-grey cliffs toward the Lantern Sea. It is a caravan, customs, and animal-remount city.","visibility":"public"}
{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Orovant makes glass, lenses, instruments, and blue ceramics using desert-edge sand and caravan fuel.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"settlement","status":"active","summary":"Tessa is a seasonal royal city of pale stone, wind courts, horse markets, observatories, and broad public cisterns. The court moves here for clear summer skies.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Managed oak woodland supplying bridge beams, charcoal, pannage, and the kingdom\u0027s slowest official hunting lodge. Present pressure: Foresters and villagers dispute emergency cutting after storm damage.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A small river landing for honey, medicinal herbs, and cheap pottery, perfumed by marsh mallow and woodsmoke. Present pressure: Barges refuse to stop after three crews report a singing light beneath the pilings.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A shallow cattle crossing, cider hamlet, and eel-smoking stop where every fence leans in the same prevailing wind. Present pressure: A new upstream weir has deepened the ford and stranded the autumn drove.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"region","status":"active","summary":"Chalk sheep country dotted with round barrows and generations of lost coat buttons gathered by children after rain. Present pressure: Sinkholes are opening along the wool road.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Seasonal cloth-and-food market held in roofed lanes; stallholders wear indigo aprons to show neutral trading status. Present pressure: A ceremonial apron has been stolen before treaty negotiations.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Rural workshop producing fine window glass and maintaining mulberry hedges for silk moths. Present pressure: Night moths gather in impossible numbers around one furnace.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Terraced orchard village reached by a stair-road wide enough for one mule and two strongly held opinions. Present pressure: Fruit trees flower twice and exhaust themselves before harvest.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A roadside pavilion where orchard workers wait out storms, exchange songs, and leave jars of preserved fruit. Present pressure: Someone replaces friendly messages with threatening prophecies.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Salt terraces descending to tidal pans, worked by extended households in mirrored light. Present pressure: An unusual tide spoils the season\u0027s first harvest.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Cliff hospice and signal station caring for wreck survivors regardless of flag. Present pressure: A rescued stranger refuses to identify a ship no lookout saw sink.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A crowded fishing island whose houses wear blue roof tiles salvaged from wrecks. Present pressure: Two elected harbour speakers both possess apparently valid seals.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Inland ship-timber yard and tavern where retired captains command imaginary fleets over bowls of stew. Present pressure: Carefully seasoned masts disappear without wagon tracks.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Peat-cutting upland of black stone shelters, hard rain, and tiny white flowers used in miners\u0027 funerals. Present pressure: A peat fire burns underground and vents beside isolated homes.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Reservoir village maintaining sluices for mines and winter mills; every doorway displays a carved wooden latch. Present pressure: Someone opens the upper gate at night, wasting scarce water.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A forge hamlet recycling worn tools and battlefield iron beneath a rook colony that mimics hammer rhythms. Present pressure: Finished blades crack despite good workmanship.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A narrow pass with an inn built around a bent pine said to have supported a wandering saint. Present pressure: An avalanche has closed the official road while an escort company monopolizes the safer goat path.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"High pasture village whose elected goat judge settles grazing disputes beneath a painted canopy. Present pressure: Prize animals vanish and return wearing unfamiliar bells.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Slate quarry where each work call returns in a distinct echo used to measure the cliff. Present pressure: One echo has vanished, making blasting unsafe.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"A steep freight railway of ropes, brakes, and timber sledges run by a cooperative of miners\u0027 families. Present pressure: Brake ropes have been cut three times.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Modest mineral baths used by miners, pilgrims, aching nobles, and relentless local gossips. Present pressure: The spring cools during the busiest healing season.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Hilltop courier station breeding small hardy horses and drying purple flowers for safe medicinal trade. Present pressure: Messages arrive resealed but apparently unread.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Neutral meadow where nine carved posts mark grazing, court, market, and muster rights for different marches. Present pressure: A tenth post appears overnight with convincing weathering.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Roofless border manor where travelers still follow elaborate guest customs preserved by its caretaker family. Present pressure: Armed claimants demand the keys to a house with no doors.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Wagon-repair settlement built around a spring and a circular common where axle-makers test their work. Present pressure: Travelers arrive with wheels failing in the same peculiar way.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Fortified bakery and refuge storing grain against snow closures; loaves are stamped like little shields. Present pressure: Its flour reserve is infested just before winter.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Vineyard and ore-washing terraces where runoff stains stone green beneath dry-season storms. Present pressure: Crops fail below a newly reopened wash channel.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Caravanserai at a pass where travelers hang one unused saddle in memory of those lost to winter. Present pressure: Someone removes saddles bearing particular family marks.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Remote pottery works whose cooling vents make conversational sounds in mountain wind. Present pressure: Workers hear specific names whispered before accidents.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Fruit trees grow on narrow levees around the upper frame of a submerged stone doorway. Present pressure: Divers seeking treasure destabilize the levee.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Raised monastery studying fever seasons, drainage, and inexpensive nets amid relentless buzzing. Present pressure: Stored remedies are missing while nearby families fall ill.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Dry-season cattle market and dye stop with orange awnings visible for miles across the flats. Present pressure: A prized breeding ox apparently predicts which bidder will die.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Delta settlement famous for communal kitchens and three enormous wooden serving spoons carried during floods. Present pressure: One neighbourhood refuses the evacuation signal.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Mud-brick landing for scribes\u0027 ink, fish oil, reeds, and legal couriers, notorious for black-stained cats. Present pressure: Official documents fade to blank within days.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Shaded caravan court where fruit sellers, petition writers, and musicians share a long cistern. Present pressure: The cistern tastes of copper and rumors blame a curse.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Small island courthouse and ferry inn that hears cases when the Aur changes local boundaries. Present pressure: The island is drifting downstream faster than precedent allows.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Riverbank farming strip where every boundary curves around a channel that no longer exists. Present pressure: Surveyors arrive to straighten titles and displace tenant families.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Tiny island where every household keeps a bell rescued from another ship or shore. Present pressure: One bell\u0027s original owners arrive with a royal order for its return.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Narrow sea passage guided by shore needles, tide boards, and hereditary rowing pilots. Present pressure: The current reverses at the wrong hour.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Fishing village, citrus garden, and storm refuge where boats return through floating orange peels. Present pressure: Nets fill with carefully folded paper boats instead of fish.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Roofless royal retreat abandoned after every architect disagreed, now used for weddings and public theatre. Present pressure: A noble claims one completed room as private property during festival week.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Roadside inn founded where a League chair once slept through a vote; meetings there cannot exceed one hour. Present pressure: Delegates exploit the rule to prevent testimony from remote villages.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Merchant-funded toll bridge whose fee drops at sunset, producing a daily race of carts and insults. Present pressure: The bridge keeper abolishes the discount without council authority.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Courtyard where spice brokers use coloured glass tubes to compare powders without revealing recipes. Present pressure: Every sample smells faintly of smoke and buyers suspect adulteration.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Neutral bonded store with four visible buildings and a famous joke about the missing fifth. Present pressure: Inventories show goods entering a warehouse no one can find.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Sheltered highland orchard producing small pale fruit and hosting astronomers during clear winters. Present pressure: Every telescope points slightly wrong despite careful calibration.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Windy plateau where couriers test signal kites and families dry cheese in woven cages. Present pressure: Kites return with extra knots that resemble military code.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Caravan water stop whose iron-rich spring stains every drinking cup rust-red. Present pressure: The flow dwindles as three caravans converge.","visibility":"public"}

{"kind":"site","status":"active","summary":"Thousands of shallow steps carry pilgrims, salt, and pack animals over a high pass. Present pressure: Sections have been rearranged, sending travelers in circles.","visibility":"public"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Her abdication may have been conditional on permanent village appeal rights omitted from court copies.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Later royal histories call one camp ancestral rulers, though burial goods suggest equal partners.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"The seeds came from several distant valleys, evidence of wider migration than court genealogies admit.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Kitchen workers secretly kept tools and enforced the truce when nobles tried to leave.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Surviving oar marks include Selucian patterns, contradicting nationalist versions on both shores.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"A court clerk quietly altered deadlines, preventing arrests, then vanished from records.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Moor villages supplied hidden lamps but were excluded from the military epic because several were rebel sympathizers.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"It may have been an organized evacuation from something below the fells, not a trade road.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Officials later credited a duke who arrived after the rescue and took ownership of the incline.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Tool marks suggest they were practical sound barriers protecting settlements from dangerous resonances.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"The caretaker deliberately seated officers by childhood nickname so they recognized kinship ties.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"One community was erased from later charters after sheltering refugees deemed rebels.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Several members survived, deserted the war, and built lives under new names.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The deliveries may have begun as disaster relief to isolated miners before being reinterpreted as dragon tribute.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Seed jars may contain crops from a cooler climate and evidence that the \u201Cfirst\u201D delta settlers arrived later.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Water captains hid them with quiet royal consent so emergency grain would not be seized for debt.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Reactive ink may have deliberately vanished after signatories fulfilled a temporary arrangement.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"The platform was also designed to escape rulers who tried to seize the court.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"They rescued its crew and received the bell freely, while the mainland record calls it salvage theft.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Measurements in its one completed room encode how island levies were meant to rotate.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Merchants later preserved its exemption for private profit long after the emergency.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Later chairmen removed the meal-pause clause to shorten testimony from distant communities.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Its original horizon markers point toward a mountain now absent from maps and perhaps removed by ancient collapse.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}
{"status":"active","summary":"Shepherd clans supplied most labour in exchange for toll exemptions later narrowed by scribes.","provenance":"Caldris history and lore atlas","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Winter Sharing","summary":"Camps along the Mere exchanged smoked fish, flint, and shelter during a severe winter. Present consequence: Competing museums claim the Button Hills storehouses; descendants want a shared memorial instead.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-1000000000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"First Footprints","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"Seeds Beneath Ash","summary":"Charred pear and quince seeds show people replanted orchards after a volcanic haze darkened summers. Present consequence: Orchard blight revives debate over sharing protected old rootstock.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-1000000000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"First Footprints","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Feast Without Knives","summary":"Rival orchard lords negotiated irrigation rights at a feast where all knives were locked away. Present consequence: Their descendants possess an overlooked right to witness water treaties.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-700000000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"Lantern Concord","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Forty Oars","summary":"Forty crews rescued a coastal settlement after an earthquake-driven wave. Present consequence: Brinewife\u0027s Steps reveals the shared compact and possible mutual harbour rights.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-850000000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"River Thrones","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Grain Fleet Refusal","summary":"Shipwrights refused to launch unsafe grain vessels despite royal pressure during famine. Present residues: royal law, layered local rights, city charters, noble titles, border monasteries, and the common belief that each current polity is older and more inevitable than it really is.","provenance":"Caldris world bible \u2014 seven eras","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"c. 840\u2013116 BS. The Concord began as mutual protection for merchants, pilgrims, and messengers. It standardized measures, seals, road maintenance, maritime signals, debt arbitration, and the safety of certain archives. Over centuries it accumulated land, courts, armed escorts, hostage guarantees, and the power to declare whose records counted. It never formally called itself an empire. Its critics did. The Concord linked both continents and created many roads, lighthouses, script traditions, and legal concepts still used today. It also turned obligations into inheritable instruments, displaced communities whose claims could not be expressed in its forms, and learned to hide coercion inside neutral procedure. Present residues: Lantern Roads, seven-sided seals, archive houses, standard bridge widths, international guest-right, suspiciously similar court vocabulary, and dormant debt clauses.","provenance":"Caldris world bible \u2014 seven eras","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Bell Above the Water","summary":"A destructive flood shifted the crossing near the site of modern Bramblebridge. {"status":"active","title":"The Salt Petition","summary":"Storms and the loss of several coastal cargoes drove up the price of inland salt. A trading association secured exclusive access to the usable winter route, arguing that dependable escorts required dependable revenue. For a time it delivered exactly what it promised. {"status":"active","title":"The Orchard That Could Not Grow","summary":"Harth\u0027s success encouraged neighbouring landholders to plant more fruit trees. They expected the Guest Beneath the Boughs to protect the new acreage, even though no agreement promised this. After a destructive frost, angry tenants came to the old table carrying dead branches. The Guest admitted the limits of its shelter. An orchard keeper named Tessa Brin proposed a boundary marked by twelve stones and a separate, ordinary mutual-aid store for growers outside it. The renewed compact included explicit duties for pruning, nesting strips, and sharing frost losses. Tessa also founded Boughmeet, a small grafting nursery where different orchard traditions could be compared. Farmers gradually learned which benefits came from the Guest and which came from choosing the right trees for their soil. Neither discovery made the other worthless.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-974988000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"1,861\u20131,849 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Three Daughters of the River","summary":"Three small riverside lordships entered a marriage settlement intended to stop recurring toll raids. The alliance failed as a family arrangement but succeeded as an administrative one: its toll stations continued sharing escort costs after two marriages ended and the third heir joined a religious house. Queen Ceryn of House Keld assembled those arrangements into the Kingdom of Low Vey, a narrow river kingdom reaching toward Veymouth. The title sounded grander than the realm. Ceryn could compel service along the river much more reliably than in villages a day\u0027s walk into the woods. Her reign established marked navigation poles, an appeals court that travelled by boat, and a store of emergency rope and timber at major crossings. These measures made her popular with boat crews and expensive to obey for woodland tenants required to supply the timber.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-981820800,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"1,874\u20131,862 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Founding of Alderwake Fair","summary":"Where the orchard branch met an eastern drovers\u0027 track, a landholder granted four days of seasonal market peace. Herds could rest on common ground; debts could be disputed before witnesses; no participant could be arrested for an old private feud until the market closed. The settlement that grew around this bargain was called Alderwake. Its first fairwarden, Ysolde Fen, rented stalls by frontage rather than by the seller\u0027s birthplace. Foreign traders welcomed the rule. Local traders discovered that impartiality felt less admirable when it introduced competition. Musicians, animal healers, cooks, and cheap lodging followed. A fair visitor could buy wool, learn a new dance, and hear an entirely inaccurate description of the sea before noon. Couples began timing marriages to the fair because relatives from several valleys could attend.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-988653600,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"1,887\u20131,875 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Autumn Without a Debt","summary":"Aveline Sere\u0027s obligation to bring a guest to the Seventh Hearth ended with the preceding century. {"status":"active","title":"The Meeting of Three Widows","summary":"At a reed-market landing, three women whose households had lost boats formed a shared reserve to support replacement craft and bereaved families. {"status":"active","title":"The Island of the Wrong Stars","summary":"Three vessels approaching the small island of Veyr\u0027s Lantern, north of the usual Morrow Strait crossing, reported star reflections on water covered by cloud. A wreck followed when a captain trusted the reflected pattern more than his pilot\u0027s warning. The island held an abandoned observing court fitted with dark glass tiles. Earlier damage had tilted part of it toward a tidal pool. On particular nights, a surviving enchantment projected an old recorded arrangement of stars across the water. It had once been an instructional device; in its altered setting, it became a navigational hazard. Pilot Soren Avet and glassworker Dima Rell led an expedition to screen the reflecting surface and recover inscriptions. They left much of the buried court undisturbed because their hired boat could not remain through the next weather change.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-600235200,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"1,148\u20131,136 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Queen of the Second Table","summary":"The final Sorne sovereign of Highmead died after a reign marked by disputed levies and a failed succession arrangement. The most credible claimant, Queen Maressa of House Merrow, secured recognition through renewed estate agreements and the support of several market councils. Maressa held formal audiences at the great table of her predecessors. She also kept a smaller table near the household kitchens where petitioners with urgent practical complaints could be heard. Its usefulness depended on her time and judgement, not an automatic right of access available to everyone. She confirmed selected common rights, paid down part of the crown\u0027s arrears, and accepted that some collectors appointed by her own supporters should be removed. House Sorne survived as several lesser families. Highmead\u0027s crown continued under a new household, rather than requiring one dynasty to govern unchanged through every century.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-607068000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"1,161\u20131,149 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Road of Bitter Leaves","summary":"Caravans from Serevan\u0027s eastern neighbour, the Principality of Selvar, began attending the markets at Istravel in greater numbers. They brought a dried leaf brewed into a bitter, fragrant drink, alongside dyestuffs, woven mats, and pottery well suited to long transport. The drink\u0027s popularity spread first among affluent households and people working late in counting rooms. Most Chalklands villages still preferred familiar herbs or ordinary ale. An expensive imported taste did not immediately become a universal custom. Rima Dast, a Selvari carrier who owned three mules with two relatives, kept a route book describing wells, guesthouses, and the difference between advertised shelter and a dry place to sleep. She made good money for several years, then lost much of it when buyers favoured a fashionable rival district\u0027s leaves.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-613900800,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"1,174\u20131,162 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Lantern at the End of the Pier","summary":"At Leth Sarai, an elderly lamplighter named Faris Nemm maintained a small light on a disused pier because his brother\u0027s boat had once returned there in a fog. After Faris died, the light appeared on several evenings when nobody admitted tending it. A small spirit had settled in the lamp housing, accustomed to the repeated act of welcome. {"status":"active","summary":"Harth\u0027s Guest woke briefly during preparations for a wedding near its root ground. It recognised the feast layout and assumed an old obligation was being renewed.
