{"status":"active","title":"The Duke Who Counted Empty Beds","summary":"In an outlying Roven district, Duke Samel of Reth claimed that hearth taxes undercounted people living seasonally along the pack routes. His collectors began charging for beds available to travellers as if each represented a permanent household. The policy made shelter expensive and encouraged hosts to remove bedding before inspections. Winter carriers arrived to find rooms technically empty and practically useless. Host Talia Penn, supported by hauliers and several judges, challenged the interpretation through the district\u0027s own agreements. The settlement distinguished seasonal lodging from permanent residence and established a smaller, visible contribution toward road support. Reth remained a northern jurisdiction outside Highmead\u0027s direct authority; the Court of Seven Roads could provide examples and witnesses, not dictate the outcome.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-344268000,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"661\u2013649 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Lord Beneath the Rushes","summary":"Boat crews working a neglected reed channel reported attacks by a long, low creature that could pull an unwary person from a landing. Locals called it the Rush Lord after seeing reeds and old netting draped across its back. The creature was an unusually large marsh predator occupying sheltered water near a collapsed fish weir. Stories gave it tribute, subjects, and a treasury. In practice, workers had begun leaving fish scraps to distract it, teaching it to approach occupied landings for food. Reed cutter Bellan Ose and hunter Ira Thenn organised safer access, removed the accumulated scraps, and mapped its routes. After repeated attacks continued, a guarded party trapped and killed it at a confined side channel. Reopening the neglected waterway took much longer than the hunt.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-351100800,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"674\u2013662 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Glassmaker\u0027s Daughter and the False Relics","summary":"Collectors were paying high prices for anything plausibly connected to Aveline. In Istravel, glassworker Yamina Rell found that an ordinary marked reference blank from an old workshop collection had been advertised as Aveline\u0027s last enchanted mirror. Comparison with Fenn Arul\u0027s copied parcel research identified the kind of object accurately. It might be the original reference piece or a workshop successor made to the same pattern; its continuous custody could not be proved. Yamina\u0027s account separated the identification of a tool from certainty about one particular object\u0027s history. The controversy exposed several other false relics, but not every seller was knowingly dishonest. Some had inherited confident descriptions and never examined them. {"status":"active","title":"The Court of Seven Roads","summary":"Highmead\u0027s King Neral Merrow convened representatives from seven established road districts to address escorts, duplicate collections, and recurring disputes over maintenance. {"status":"active","title":"The Mile of Little Bridges","summary":"Repeated washouts on the approach to Goat\u0027s Ledger made carriers propose one expensive raised causeway. {"status":"active","title":"The Convoy That Waited for Rain","summary":"A convoy leaving the Serevan coast faced pressure to sail before an approaching seasonal change. {"status":"active","title":"The Evening Market of Brinefold","summary":"Brinefold set aside a quay-side yard for the sale of used equipment, small return cargoes, and household goods. {"status":"active","title":"Salt Without Sails","summary":"A dispute over harbour charges on the Serevan coast led several merchant houses to withhold sailings. Officials expected a short concession struggle. Instead, the interruption lasted through an important preserving season, raising salt prices in some inland markets while salt workers near idle quays struggled to sell their stock. Caravan organiser Dema Noll arranged smaller shipments through secondary landings and inland roads. The journeys were costly and exposed carriers to theft. Some officials tolerated them; others seized goods to demonstrate that the embargo still meant something. The eventual settlement reduced selected charges and changed how harbour repairs were funded. The temporary routes did not all disappear. A handful of overlooked villages acquired inns, workshops, and customers, while the older route lost part of its dependable trade.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-134290800,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"259\u2013252 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Birds in Cinder Meadow","summary":"A dry-season fire crossed part of Boughmeet\u0027s nursery country. Growers saved cuttings and tools, but several plots burned. During the first rains, witnesses saw slender birds with ember-bright throats searching the ash. Their footprints cooled into faint glassy impressions in exposed sand. Nursery keeper Pera Elven fenced a small nesting patch rather than allowing collectors to chase the birds through newly planted ground. Most departed within weeks. One pair remained until its young could fly, and the damaged plot acquired the name Cinder Meadow. The nursery recovered through ordinary planting and exchanged stock. The birds became a symbol of renewal, although their appearance had neither prevented the fire nor restored the lost trees. Families whose livelihoods had burned did not all welcome cheerful songs about the disaster.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-138495600,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"267\u2013260 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Opening of Ashglass House","summary":"In Istravel, glassmaker Sena Dorr and mage Arvel Senn founded Ashglass House, a workshop specialising in the repair and repurposing of small enchanted glass objects. {"status":"active","title":"The Tables Kept for Strangers","summary":"Hosts along several northern and coastal routes adopted a modest agreement to keep a few places available for delayed carriers during difficult weather. Host Sera Kell coordinated the first surviving set of reciprocal promises, accepting that some houses would provide more shelter than they received in return. Elsewhere it endured through revised contributions and limits clearly explained to travellers. At two hundred years ago, a marked table could mean a chance to wait out rain among strangers with different destinations. The custom carried stories, recipes, warnings, and songs as effectively as the freight travelling beside them.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-108010800,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"211\u2013200 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Day Little Lastlight Went Dark","summary":"Little Lastlight failed to appear at the repaired pier in Leth Sarai. {"status":"active","title":"The Hearing Beneath the Old Banner","summary":"An ageing road grant was invoked to collect payments from settlements now served by several different routes. Highmead\u0027s regional court heard claims from landholders, carriers, maintenance houses, and towns whose practical obligations had diverged over generations. Judge Tessa Dorn refused to treat the earliest document as the complete answer. The court compared later renewals, actual repair work, and agreements made by successor authorities. The resulting settlement preserved some payments, ended others, and required fresh negotiation where the evidence was contradictory. Petitioners lodged in the city for months. Bakers, hosts, and money changers benefited from the gathering, while families at home absorbed the cost of absent workers. The hearing became a political landmark and a collection of private disappointments.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-121676400,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"235\u2013228 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","title":"The Letters That Wintered Abroad","summary":"Bad weather and disrupted sailings stranded a collection of private correspondence in Leth Sarai. {"status":"active","title":"The Host Who Hung No Banner","summary":"The orc host Havra Renn opened the Lantern Hospice on a Veyr road used by carriers, pilgrims, and seasonal workers. {"status":"active","title":"The Duet Played Without Its Visitor","summary":"Nivren Sael promised to return for a small musical gathering near Three-Reed Bridge. {"status":"active","title":"The Grain Houses with Empty Lofts","summary":"Several towns paid advances for grain expected from the same producing district. {"status":"active","title":"The Toll Collected after the Repairs","summary":"A charge introduced to restore a damaged approach remained in force after the contracted work was complete. Local collectors argued that future maintenance justified retaining it. Carriers objected that the original authorisation described a temporary payment, while neighbouring crossings worried about losing traffic if they charged less. Others retained their arrangements, citing different grants or postponed work. The dispute produced a useful local precedent and no universal reform. {"status":"active","title":"Two Funerals and Many New Claims","summary":"Two unrelated royal heirs died within eighteen months of one another in separate accidents. Rumour joined the deaths into a single pattern even where the available evidence did not. They added pressure to an already complicated political landscape rather than collapsing every disputed future into one inheritance.","calendarId":"caldris-common-era","occurredAtMinute":-1051200,"precision":"era","dateLabel":"3\u20131 years ago","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"Crownroot Cathedral \u2014 Amberstile: Footpath. A signed graft-carriers\u0027 lane reaches the root court. {"status":"active","summary":"The first ripe fruit is shared after a meal rather than auctioned. A graft must be accompanied by the name of the person who tended its parent tree. Sellers rent tables by the day; they cannot purchase a permanent root alcove. No pilgrimage fee buys a promise of frost protection.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"One celebrated branch was quietly replaced after disease killed it. Its fruit is excellent, but a merchant markets it as the unchanged scion of the original compact. Exposing the claim threatens honest gardeners as well as the merchant. The Guest\u0027s limited capacity remains limited; the tree cannot be used to extend protection across all Alderwick by selling cuttings.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The old teacher returns and finds the pupil she remembers as a boy preparing to retire. A lucrative new fruit variety threatens the unharvested bird strip. Two villages each possess a sound but incompatible record of a donated branch, and both need its crop to fund their winter kitchen.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Crownroot is a later daughter sanctuary of the Orchard Compact associated with Harth, not the original compact\u0027s birthplace. Successive grafts, living root columns and repeated soil work explain much of its size; small sheltering spells supplement that labour. The Guest Beneath the Boughs has been offered a place here on several occasions, but a vast canopy is not proof that the Guest protects every nearby field. The human grafter Oswin Pell keeps an empty seat for his former elven teacher, who last visited thirty-seven years ago. Historical threads: The Orchard Compact; The Orchard that Counted Birds.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"Lanternback Colossus \u2014 Wetherfold Common: Footpath. The southern grazing track approaches the spring hand. Livestock and nesting seasons can require local detours.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"Lanternback Colossus \u2014 The White Lamb Downs: Footpath. The shepherds\u0027 chalk path reaches the open rib shelter and ends there; it does not enter the buried chambers.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"A visitor may hang one lantern for someone who helped them, but the keeper lends the lantern rather than selling ownership of a rib. The last bowl of stew goes to whoever has arrived most recently. Climbing the head is forbidden during lambing, and the deep crawlspaces beneath the spring are outside the open shelter.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The strange lantern was hung by a frightened descendant using an old family name, not by a power predicting death. Beneath the spring is a reused grain chamber containing evidence that several respectable households charged for shelter during a later famine. The chamber is structurally unsafe and has no registered open approach. The stone figure itself neither wakes nor grants wishes.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"A wealthy family offers to restore the cracked left hand if the communal hearth becomes its private memorial. A lantern bearing the name of a living traveller appears in a row usually used for the dead. Tessa needs someone to recover her first repair sketch from Highmead; without it, a well-meant new brace may obstruct the spring.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The colossus belongs to the same chalk country as the Button Hills granaries. People connect its open hearths with the Winter of Borrowed Hearths, but no surviving account proves that Maelin Rusk herself came here. A bowl is still set out for an absent guest. The dwarf mason Tessa Flintrill has returned every eleventh spring for almost a century; she recognises several families by their repaired cooking pots before she recognises their faces. Historical threads: The Winter of Borrowed Hearths; The War of False Weights.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The Skyharp grew from changes to quarry transport after the griffin crisis above Juniper Gate. Early keepers lifted supplies along the rock face to reduce disturbance near nesting slopes. When the freight machinery was retired, later porters tuned its surviving cables into audible weather signals. Different air currents can make the same note mean different things; the songs supplement observation rather than predict the future. Keeper Marra Venn knows which familiar tones are produced by worn fittings. Historical threads: The Griffin Above Juniper Gate; The Winter of Returned Keys; The Winter Latch.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Before a boat is lowered, the newest worker reads the stop signal and the oldest worker demonstrates that it still works. Hulls carry names of lost vessels, but the crew maintains a list distinguishing memorial names from original timbers. Visitors buy lunch at the cooperative table; paying for a tour does not authorise entry to a suspended work cradle.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The upper works were expanded during the Salt Without Sails disruptions, when inland and coastal shortages made repairing smaller craft more useful than waiting for a great fleet. Later generations replaced most of the original timber. Recent arguments at Gullstrand\u0027s Closed Launch revived the harbour workers\u0027 older right to refuse an unsafe lowering, making this an important witness site for the history of practical judgement and maritime labour. Historical threads: Salt Without Sails; The Hearing at the Closed Launch.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"Skyharp of Roven \u2014 Hearthscar Shelter: Footpath. A maintained ledge spur ends at the grounded harp platform. There is no crossing to Juniper Gate, Crowstep, or the Unfinished Stair from the monument.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Porters tie a ribbon for a safe return and remove an older ribbon when they come back. A novice is taught to distinguish a warning bell from a musical cable before being trusted with the platform. Silence can mean still air or broken equipment; nobody is charged a toll for hearing the harp.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"A repair using a different bronze alloy has shifted one resonator\u0027s note. That explains the false warning, but not a newly uncovered winch mark belonging to an unrecorded salvage crew. The crew\u0027s cache is on the near side of the gorge. Neither it nor the harp creates a bypass around the Unfinished Stair.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The harp sounds a retired warning while the official forecast promises clear passage. A collector offers enough money for winter supplies in exchange for the oldest resonator. A griffin is scouting the old slope again, and both convoy owners and shepherds want the keeper to call it somebody else\u0027s problem.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"The Upward Fall \u2014 Redbank Reach: Footpath. The north-bank inspection path reaches the public viewing platform and the ordinary sluice works.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"The Upward Fall \u2014 Willowrace: Footpath. A mill-workers\u0027 embankment path follows maintained ground. It never passes through the rising water or the old aqueduct gallery.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Apprentices drink from an ordinary kettle before studying the fall, to remember that useful water matters more than spectacle. The public gauge is read aloud at the morning inspection. A family may sponsor one length of repaired channel, but cannot claim the downstream water solely because its plaque stands nearest the arch.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"A recently altered garden drain, approved under an obsolete property name, accounts for most of the missing water. Nobody involved understood the whole plan. A small remaining discrepancy points to a sealed inspection pocket containing the original rejected channel proposal. The fall cannot lift travellers or provide unlimited power; attempts to enlarge the flow damage its carefully prepared bed.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Water continues to rise while the downstream gauge falls: a hidden leak or diversion is robbing someone of a promised share. A theatrical mage claims to have invented the ancient lift. The replacement mineral bed is trapped in an ownership dispute, and shutting the fall for repair will cost one village its early vegetable crop.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The fall is a surviving later experiment inspired by the Open Sluices Agreement. Its builders wanted a modest irrigation lift, not a wall against every flood. The first spell depended on a prepared mineral bed that still needs renewal. During heavy flooding the keepers close the diversion because the arch and receiving channel cannot safely handle the additional water. Halda Penn\u0027s name appears in later arguments about the work, but she did not approve every project subsequently built in her memory. Historical threads: The Agreement of the Open Sluices; The Spring of Floating Doors.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"Emberglass Whale \u2014 Var Keth: Footpath. The assayers\u0027 terrace path ends at the public jaw platform. The fragile rib interior and tail scaffold are not onward routes.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"Visitors borrow tinted viewing tiles to watch sunlight travel through the ribs. A chip is never taken as a souvenir; licensed makers sell copies from their own furnaces. Traders leave one jar of water for the return climb, an ordinary courtesy at a monument shaped like a creature of the sea.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The whale\u0027s hollow ribs once demonstrated differences in furnace temperatures and sound, combining art with a teaching instrument. Its joined construction was obscured by later glazing. The missing pattern is an old repair key rather than a prophecy. Karsh did not make the whale, and its existence neither proves the old tithe was legitimate nor cancels real obligations arising elsewhere.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"A collector produces a fragment that appears to complete a pattern absent from every published drawing. A new copper claim would require a cart road beneath the tail. Someone sells accurate copies as relics, but the workshop making them needs the income to repair the genuine monument.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"gm"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The whale was already damaged when Kethrian accounts first describe it. During the Sleeper Opens One Eye period, some officials tried to present it as evidence that all local glasswork belonged to the sleeping dragon\u0027s tithe. Later assayers challenged that convenient claim. The false-relic controversies of later centuries sent carved splinters abroad under extravagant labels. Guide Iven Sar keeps genuine repair fragments beside cheap copies and explains why either may still be beautiful. Historical threads: The Sleeper Opens One Eye; The Glassmaker\u0027s Daughter and the False Relics.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; reconciled with the existing chronology before campaign play.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"The Hanging Harbour \u2014 Saltmere: Boat passage. A boat passage reaches the lower landing when the swell and the harbour keeper permit. No on-foot journey is registered for this water connection.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"archived","summary":"The Hanging Harbour \u2014 Gullstrand: Footpath. A maintained cliff-top path reaches the inspected upper yard. It grants no automatic access to moving cradles or the lower hoist.","provenance":"Nine Wonders of Caldris; named present-day access.","visibility":"public"}

{"status":"active","summary":"The chain was substituted by a supplier trying to keep an underpaid workshop solvent, not by a foreign saboteur. The material is unsafe for the heaviest cradle. Records hidden in a patched rib also show that the cooperative once accepted a profitable priority repair that delayed a poorer community\u0027s boat.
